description:
tests/filenode_tests.rs has 9 integration tests covering create/destroy/cascade/get/fetchParents/query/changes. None of them assert on the response 'oldState' or 'newState' fields, or on the FileNodeBackend invariant 'State monotonicity: get_state returns a different token after every successful mutation. Token does not change on failure.' (PLAN.md line 100-101).

A regression where the backend forgets to bump state on a mutation (or bumps it twice, or returns stale state) would pass every existing test. The state invariant is the foundation of FileNode/changes correctness — without state monotonicity, clients cannot detect missed updates.

Suggested test additions:
1. After a successful create: assert resp['newState'] != resp['oldState'].
2. After a failed create (e.g., invalid name): assert resp['newState'] == resp['oldState'].
3. After a mixed-success /set (one create succeeds, one fails): assert the state moved exactly once.
4. After FileNode/changes with sinceState=newState: assert empty deltas (no further changes).

These tests would have caught the JMAP-510h.4 (query_subtree silent truncation) class of bug at integration level if combined with a 'state moved means changes log has entries' invariant check.
title: Integration tests do not assert on oldState/newState transitions across mutations
